FICTIONAL EXAMPLE DOCUMENT. The materials, laboratories and measurements below are invented for software testing.

Effect of electrolyte purity on nickel-based oxygen evolution catalysts

Summary. Trace iron in commercial potassium hydroxide is known to change the activity of nickel oxyhydroxides. We quantified this effect for unmodified nickel hydroxide films.

Method. Films were tested in reagent-grade 1 M KOH and in the same electrolyte after purification over nickel hydroxide powder to remove iron. Iron content was measured before each test.

Results. In unpurified KOH containing 0.6 ppm iron, the overpotential at 10 mA cm-2 decreased by 80 mV over the first hour as iron was incorporated into the film. In purified KOH the overpotential remained high and nearly constant.

Implication. Durability and activity comparisons between laboratories are only meaningful if the electrolyte iron content is reported. This study did not examine LX-4 or any intentionally iron-doped catalyst.
